the expression of lamins A, B and C is altered in lung cancer cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of lamins A, B and C in the pathogenesis of lung cancers.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the development of lung cancer.
the role of nuclear envelope proteins in the regulation of cell function and with the relationship between changes in these proteins and changes in cell phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lamina is an important component of nuclear structure and that the lamins are expressed in a phenotype-specific manner in lung cancer.
the expression of lamins is not related to the type of lung cancer, but it is related to the phenotype of the cell.
the expression of lamins in human lung cancer cells is not only different in the different cell lines but also in the same cell line depending on the oncogenic state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of nuclear envelope lamin proteins in human lung cancer cells is correlated with the phenotype of the cells.
the v-ras H gene induces a change in nuclear lamina structure that may be related to the change in phenotype from small cell lung cancer to large cell lung cancer.
the lamins, an abundant class of nuclear envelope proteins, are expressed in a cell-type-specific fashion in human lung cancer lines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear envelope is a highly dynamic structure that can change in response to oncogenic transformation.
lamin A and C expression is down-regulated in small cell lung cancer cell lines, and this may be due to the loss of the lamin A gene promoter in small cell lung carcinoma.
the nuclear envelope is not just a static structure, but is dynamic and changes with cell type.
